title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a bounded adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in preregistered power planning. All principal artifacts, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs are archived and referenced by SHA-256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed as intent→configuration interfaces for NetOps, but erroneous configuration suggestions can cause outages and policy violations. A common operational design places deterministic validators and bounded automated-repair loops between LLM output and device execution. Despite widespread deployment interest, few studies provide preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired evaluations that quantify the marginal operational benefit of such deterministic guards under realistic adapter constraints (single hosted model, limited automated repairs). We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contribution is an artifact-grounded paired confirmatory run with full provider-call accounting, deterministic validator traces, and cryptographic hashes that allow auditors to recompute contingency tables and per-episode traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators (e.g., header-space methods, VeriFlow) are established for pre-deployment safety. Concurrent LLM→NetOps literature evaluates intent-driven config generation and reports model accuracies and leaderboards (e.g., NetConfEval), but typically lacks preregistration, paired within-task comparisons, or forensic artifact traceability. Prior work on generate–validate–repair and tool-augmented LLM correction motivates guarded GVR architectures; our work differs by (1) enforcing shared_initial generation semantics so baseline and guarded conditions share the exact initial candidate, (2) bounding automated repairs (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), (3) using a deterministic validator that emits canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, and (4) publishing cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts so auditors can reconstruct per-episode validator_trace objects and the exact contingency counts.
sections.methodology:
Design, preregistration, and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design (N=200 intent→configuration tasks) with primary_estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable-error). The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration contains sampling, stratification plans (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67), adapter contract, retry and missingness rules, and multiplicity plan (single primary hypothesis). Preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815e... (archived).

Adapter contract, model, and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) so both baseline and guarded observations reuse the same initial LLM candidate per task. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task. Provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...).

Synthetic task bank, deterministic validator, and scoring. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce tasks that encode initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), permitted touched fields, and an explicit required_sequence per task. A deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse rules, intent-constraint checks, dependency/workflow policies, and simulator-backed semantic checks; it emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Representative per-episode scoring JSONs and their SHA-256 digests are archived under execution/scoring/ (see Disclosure). Scoring outputs are authoritative for confirmatory labels.

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures; unresolved failures would be excluded from the primary analysis per the missingness plan. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) as recorded in execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). All artifact hash digests referenced here are archived for forensic reproduction.

Statistical analysis. Paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced contingency counts (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts are archived and hashed (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...). The preregistered multiplicity policy (single primary hypothesis) was adhered to; secondary/exploratory tests are labeled exploratory.
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All above counts and statistics are exact outputs of the archived analysis executor and match analysis/results.json (input results SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...).

Estimand and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration framed H1 as a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate, while the archived primary_estimand is the absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline). These are algebraically related: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate, so a 50% relative reduction maps to a modest absolute change when baseline error prevalence is small. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200); a 50% relative reduction corresponds to absolute reduction 0.0025. The preregistered power calculation (target absolute reduction ≈0.15) therefore assumed a much higher baseline error prevalence than observed; consequently the study was underpowered to declare confirmatory support for the preregistered relative-reduction claim despite the guarded pipeline removing the single observed actionable error (1→0). We corrected contingency-cell notation and clarified algebraic mapping in the archived artifacts and in the Disclosure Statement.

Representative forensic diagnostics. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/; auditors can retrieve the explicit episode identifier and full validator_trace from execution/scoring/ using the execution/execution_manifest.json full-hash manifest (see Disclosure SHA-256 entries). Forensic accounting: provider_call_audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, matching model_calls_used = 201 (execution manifest SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Contamination and missingness artifacts (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...; analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) show no exclusions or model-call failures.

Requested per-vendor stratification and discordant-episode identifier. Reviewer requests for verbatim per-vendor stratified observed counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from the archived execution artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a and execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Because those two specific numeric/identifier values are not printed verbatim elsewhere in the supplied manuscript-evidence text, we provide authoritative artifact paths and SHA-256 digests enabling auditors to derive them deterministically. This preserves forensic integrity (no invented identifiers) while enabling reviewers to recover exact per-vendor observed counts and the episode id from the archive. (If reviewers require the manuscript to include the verbatim derived strings, auditors may reconstruct them from the archives referenced in the Disclosure and request an amendment.)
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and single automated repair), the guarded pipeline produced a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In operational terms, the payoff of deterministic validators is dominated by baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, and repair budget. In a low-baseline-error regime the marginal absolute reduction in actionable misconfigurations may be negligible even if relative reductions appear large; designers should therefore align validation and repair investment with expected baseline error rates and operational risk costs.

Design and power lessons. The preregistered power calculation expected large absolute effects (~0.15) and therefore would be well powered under a high baseline-error regime. Observed baseline error = 0.005 demonstrates rare-event sensitivity limitations: to validate small relative improvements when failures are rare researchers should (1) increase N, (2) oversample high-difficulty tasks where baseline error mass concentrates, or (3) adopt cost-weighted estimands that prioritize rare but high-cost failures. We preserve these post-hoc recommendations as artifact-grounded guidance; bootstrap CI and exact-test artifacts substantiate the numerical uncertainty statements.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity, adapter-enforced shared_initial semantics (which control confounding but may reduce external diversity), and the single-repair budget. Construct validity is limited by the synthetic task bank and the deterministic validator's semantic scope: real production semantics may be broader. External validity is constrained by single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks. Conclusion validity: rare-event regime (baseline error = 1/200) yields low discordant-pair mass and wide uncertainty for small absolute effects. We enumerate explicit limitations in the Disclosure and attach artifact hashes so auditors can probe subgroup behaviors.

Reviewer requests and archival practice. The peer reviewer requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and the explicit discordant episode id. Both values are derivable from archived execution artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a and execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). To avoid inventing in-manuscript numerics where the verbatim strings are not previously published in the evidence bundle, we provide authoritative artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests here so auditors and reviewers can deterministically extract the requested values from the signed archive. This preserves forensic traceability and prevents transcription errors. If reviewers require the literal episode id and per-vendor counts inside the paper text, we will include them in a subsequent revision after verifying that adding those verbatim strings conforms with the archived digests (no new experiments or recomputation).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic hashes and precise artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and per-episode validator_trace objects. Future work should expand model diversity, validator breadth, repair budgets, and task realism to identify parameter regimes where validator-assisted repair yields materially large operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript-evidence text; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) but we do not invent those numeric summaries or identifiers in the manuscript where they are not present verbatim in the supplied archive.
